primary_diagnosis_treated: End-stage diabetic nephropathy (CKD stage 5 secondary to type 2 diabetes)

medications.dose: Start 1.25 mg once daily; titrate every 2 weeks to 5 mg once daily (max 10 mg) as tolerated
medications.duration: Lifelong — review renal function & potassium 1–2 weeks after each dose change, then annually
medications.purpose: Reduce intraglomerular pressure, slow proteinuric CKD progression and provide cardiovascular protection
medications.nice_justification: NG203 recommends ACE‑I for CKD with ACR ≥30 mg/mmol or hypertension; monitor creatinine & K⁺ after 1–2 weeks

medications.duration: Lifelong — review lipid profile and liver function at 3 months, then annually
medications.purpose: Cardiovascular risk reduction in CKD (equivalent to high risk)
medications.nice_justification: NG203 advises statin for all CKD patients for CV risk reduction

medications.dose: 650 mg (≈8 mmol) orally three times daily, titrate to maintain serum bicarbonate 22–26 mmol/L
medications.duration: Until serum bicarbonate target achieved, then review every 3 months
medications.purpose: Correct severe metabolic acidosis (pH 7.10) and mitigate CKD‑MBD progression
medications.nice_justification: NG203 recommends monitoring and treating bicarbonate in CKD stage 4‑5

medications.dose: 25 000 IU subcutaneously once weekly (dose adjusted to maintain Hb 10–11.5 g/dL)
medications.duration: Until hemoglobin 10–11.5 g/dL, then review every 3 months
medications.nice_justification: NG203 recommends ESA after iron repletion for CKD patients with Hb <10 g/dL

medications.dose: 0.25 µg orally once daily (adjust according to corrected calcium & phosphate)
medications.duration: Until calcium, phosphate and PTH are within target; review every 1–3 months
medications.nice_justification: NG203 advises active vitamin D for CKD‑MBD when PTH elevated

medications.dose: 5 mg orally once daily (increase to 10 mg if needed)
medications.duration: If required for BP control; lifelong with regular BP monitoring
medications.purpose: Achieve BP target <130/80 mmHg when ACE‑I alone insufficient
medications.nice_justification: NG203 non‑pharmacological target BP <130/80 mmHg for ACR ≥70 mg/mmol; CCB is recommended adjunct

medications.duration: 7 days (or oral step‑down after culture results)
medications.nice_justification: Guideline‑based infection management; avoid nitrofurantoin in eGFR <30 mL/min

interactions_checked.action: Monitor blood pressure after initiation and titration; adjust doses if symptomatic hypotension

interactions_checked.interaction: Potential for hyperkalaemia if bicarbonate causes volume expansion
interactions_checked.action: Check serum potassium 1–2 weeks after starting bicarbonate

contraindications.reason: eGFR 5 mL/min/1.73 m² (<30) – risk of lactic acidosis
eGFR 5 mL/min – would worsen renal function and raise BP
contraindications.alternative: Paracetamol for analgesia; consider low‑dose opioid if needed

contraindications.reason: Increased risk of hyperkalaemia and acute kidney injury
Nephrotoxic and cannot be dose‑adjusted at eGFR 5 mL/min
High risk of contrast‑induced nephropathy at eGFR <30
contraindications.alternative: If imaging required, use low‑osmolar non‑ionic contrast with pre‑ and post‑hydration and consider dialysis

assumptions_warnings: Baseline serum potassium, liver function tests, calcium, phosphate, PTH, and hemoglobin not provided – will be obtained before initiating ACE‑I, statin, ESA, and calcitriol.
Current antihypertensive regimen unknown – assume none; BP target will be guided by NICE BP targets.
Allergy status not recorded – will verify no ACE‑I, statin, or sulfonamide allergies before prescribing.
Exact urinary pathogen not known – empirical ceftriaxone chosen pending culture; will adjust based on sensitivities.
treatment_summary: Initiate ACE‑I (Ramipril) and high‑intensity statin (Atorvastatin) for renal protection and CV risk reduction, correct severe metabolic acidosis with sodium bicarbonate, treat CKD‑related anemia with epoetin alfa after iron repletion, manage secondary hyperparathyroidism with calcitriol, add amlodipine if BP remains above target, and treat the current UTI with a 7‑day course of ceftriaxone. All choices follow NICE NG203, avoid contraindicated drugs, and include monitoring plans.
